title: Three letters, then a Book full of wisdom.
subtitle: Pausing before a wise Book speaks
then: Late in the Makkan years, opposition to the Prophet ﷺ was at its harshest. The surah opens with three letters whose meaning is known to Allah, and then names what follows: {idea}verses of a Book whose wisdom is clear.{/idea}
now: You open the Quran app between two notifications. Your thumb is ready to scroll. Three letters sit there that you cannot explain. {idea}Let them slow you down.{/idea} Something wise is about to be said to you.
old: I read the Quran the way I read everything else, fast.
new: The opening letters are a pause button before wisdom speaks.
try: Before your next reading, put the phone face down for ten seconds, then begin.

title: Why would a messenger be one of us?
subtitle: The surprise that a man brought revelation
then: Many Arabs said Allah is too great to send a human messenger. Ibn Abbas said this verse came as the reply. {trap}When the message could not be answered, they called the Prophet ﷺ a sorcerer.{/trap} Yet he was one of their own, sent to warn and to give {reward}good news.{/reward}
now: Advice from a stranger with a big title feels serious. The same advice from your cousin, your coworker, your mother, gets a shrug. {trap}Familiar means easy to ignore.{/trap} Sometimes the truth arrives wearing a face you already know.
old: If the message came through someone ordinary, it cannot be that important.
new: Allah chose a human so the message could be lived, not just admired.
try: Think of good advice you brushed off because of who said it. Take it seriously today.

title: The One who runs everything deserves your worship.
subtitle: Creator, ruler, and the only one to worship
then: The people of Makkah admitted Allah created the heavens and the earth. Yet they worshipped other gods hoping those would plead for them. Ibn Kathir notes {idea}no request of His creatures troubles Him, and He governs small things as He governs big ones.{/idea} So the verse asks: {trap}will you not remember?{/trap}
now: Your rent, your test result, your visa, your child's fever. You may be lining up people to pull strings for you. {idea}The One who arranges every affair is not too busy for yours.{/idea} Ask Him first.
old: My problem is too small for Allah, so I chase people who can fix it.
new: He governs every detail, so I can bring Him the small things too.
try: Pick one small worry you have not prayed about. Ask Allah about it, plainly, today.

title: Everyone goes back to Him, and justice is waiting.
subtitle: The return of all creation and its fair outcome
then: Quraysh doubted that the dead would rise. The verse answers: the One who began creation will repeat it. Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}no one will be left out{/idea}, and the reward for faith and good deeds will be {reward}full and just.{/reward} Those who rejected face {trap}a painful outcome.{/trap}
now: You did the right thing at work and nobody noticed. Someone cut a corner and got promoted. It feels like nothing adds up. {idea}The account is not closed yet.{/idea} Every deed returns with you.
old: If nobody saw it, it did not count.
new: Everything returns to Allah, and He rewards with full justice.
try: Do one good thing today that no one will ever know about.

title: The sun and moon are a calendar with a purpose.
subtitle: Light, phases, and counting time
then: The listeners lived by the moon. Ibn Kathir describes it starting thin, growing full, then shrinking back each month. {idea}The days come from the sun, the months and years from the moon.{/idea} None of it was made {trap}for amusement.{/trap}
now: You check your calendar app, your payday countdown, the date of Ramadan. Every one of those numbers rests on a sun and a moon that never miss. {idea}Time itself was given to you on purpose.{/idea}
old: The sky is just there, and time just passes.
new: The sun and moon were set up so I can count my days, and my days are counted.
try: Look at the moon tonight and guess its phase. Then thank Allah for one day you had this month.

title: Night and day keep swapping, and that is a sign.
subtitle: Signs that only the mindful notice
then: Ibn Kathir describes night and day following each other {idea}with no errors{/idea}, one arriving as the other leaves. The signs are everywhere, but the verse says they speak to {reward}people who are mindful of Allah.{/reward}
now: Your alarm goes off in the dark and you are home before sunset in winter. The switch happens every single day and you have never once looked up for it. {idea}The sign was there. Attention was missing.{/idea}
old: Sunrise and sunset are just background.
new: The steady swap of night and day speaks to anyone who is paying attention to Allah.
try: Watch one sunset or sunrise today, start to finish, without your phone.

title: Content with this world, and not expecting to meet Him.
subtitle: The quiet comfort that makes a person heedless

row.title: no hope of meeting
sub: the Day is not real to them

then: Al-Hasan said they {trap}decorated this world and praised it until they were satisfied with it.{/trap} They did not reflect on the signs around them, and did not follow Allah's laws. The meeting with Allah was simply not on their mind.
now: The new car, the renovated kitchen, the holiday booked for next summer. None of it is wrong. {trap}The danger is feeling fully settled{/trap}, as if this place is home and there is no one to meet after it.
old: If my life is comfortable, I must be doing fine.
new: Comfort is a blessing, but feeling settled in it can make me forget the meeting.
try: Today, when you enjoy something nice, say quietly: this is not my final home.

title: Where you end up is what you earned.
subtitle: The outcome follows the life that was lived
then: This continues the previous verse. Ibn Kathir says their abode is {trap}a recompense for the sins they earned in their worldly life{/trap}, on top of rejecting Allah, His Messenger ﷺ, and the Last Day. {idea}The ending matches the path.{/idea}
now: Small habits compound. Five minutes of scrolling becomes three hours. A skipped prayer becomes a skipped week. {idea}Today is still the earning season.{/idea} You can change what you are collecting.
old: One small habit does not decide anything.
new: My ending is built from what I earn, day by day.
try: Name one habit that is earning you something bad. Cut it once today.

title: Your faith becomes the light that guides you home.
subtitle: Belief and good deeds as a path to the Gardens
then: After the heedless, the verse turns to those who believed and did good. Mujahid said {reward}their faith will be a light in which they will walk.{/reward} Ibn Kathir adds it may mean Allah {idea}guides them to the straight path because of their faith.{/idea}
now: A dark parking lot, your phone torch lighting one step at a time. You do not see the car yet, only the next metre. {reward}Faith with action works like that.{/reward} It lights the next step, and the next.
old: Faith is a feeling I keep to myself.
new: Faith joined with good deeds becomes the light that walks me home.
try: Do one good deed today that your faith asks of you, however small.

title: In Paradise, praise comes as easily as breathing.
subtitle: The words the people of Paradise say
then: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith in Muslim: {reward}the people of Paradise will be inspired to glorify and praise Allah as they breathe.{/reward} Their greeting is peace. And their last words are {idea}praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.{/idea}
now: You hit send on a family group chat and it turns into an argument. Imagine a place where every greeting is {reward}peace{/reward} and every conversation ends with thanks. {idea}You can practise those words here.{/idea}
old: Praising Allah is something I remember to do sometimes.
new: Praise is the language of Paradise, and I can start speaking it now.
try: End today's last conversation, or your last thought before sleep, with alhamdulillah.

title: Thank Allah He does not answer your angry prayers.
subtitle: His patience with words said in anger
then: Mujahid said this is a man who, angry, says of his son or his money: {trap}O Allah, do not bless him, curse him.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains {idea}Allah does not answer such prayers out of mercy{/idea}, since they do not truly want harm. The Prophet ﷺ warned not to pray against yourselves, your children, or your wealth.
now: The kid breaks the phone screen. You snap, and words come out you would never want answered. {idea}Allah's patience caught them.{/idea} Next time, catch them yourself.
old: Words said in anger do not really matter.
new: Allah shields me from my own angry words, and I should guard them too.
try: When you feel anger rise today, swap the harsh sentence for a short dua for good.

title: We call Him in pain, then walk off when it passes.
subtitle: Remembering Allah only in hard times
then: Ibn Kathir describes a person who, in distress, {trap}prays long, in every position{/trap}, then turns away once relief comes. He cites the hadith: {reward}how wonderful is the believer, patient in hardship and grateful in ease, and good comes to him in both.{/reward}
now: The hospital corridor at 2 a.m. You prayed harder than you have in years. The scan came back clear. {trap}A month later, the prayer mat is folded away again.{/trap} The relief deserved a thank you too.
old: I pray hardest when I need something.
new: The One who answered me in pain deserves my thanks when the pain is gone.
try: Recall one hard time Allah got you through. Pray two units of thanks for it today.

title: Earlier generations had clear proofs and still refused.
subtitle: What happened to past nations who did wrong

row.title: not enough proof
sub: if only they had seen more

then: The Makkans were reminded of nations before them. Ibn Kathir says they {trap}belied the Messengers and the clear signs{/trap} brought to them. {idea}The proof was never the problem.{/idea} They were not willing to believe.
now: You already know the sleep schedule that would help, the call you should make, the apology you owe. {trap}You keep waiting for one more sign.{/trap} Maybe you have enough already.
old: I would change if I had more proof.
new: Usually the proof is clear. What is missing is my willingness.
try: Pick one thing you already know is right but keep delaying. Take the first step today.

title: Now it is your turn, and He is watching how.
subtitle: Being made successors on the earth
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith: {idea}the world is sweet and green, and Allah places you in it to see how you act.{/idea} When Umar became caliph, he recalled this verse and told himself: {trap}you have been appointed, so look at what you will do.{/trap}
now: The new job title. The first apartment in your name. The day you became a parent. {idea}Each one is a handover.{/idea} Someone held it before you. The question now is what you do with your turn.
old: This position is mine to enjoy.
new: Whatever I have been handed is a turn, and Allah is watching how I use it.
try: Look at one role you hold today and ask: how would I want this turn to look when it ends?

title: Bring us a different Quran, or change this one.
subtitle: Asking the message to fit our taste
then: Ibn Kathir describes the chiefs of Quraysh asking the Prophet ﷺ to {trap}take back this Book and bring another, or change it to a different form.{/trap} He was told to answer: {idea}I am a servant who receives commands. I only follow what is revealed to me.{/idea}
now: You love most of Islam, but one verse is inconvenient. You scroll until you find an opinion that softens it. {trap}Bring me a version that fits.{/trap} The verse asks you to adjust yourself instead of the message.
old: I will take the parts that suit me and wait for the rest to change.
new: The message is not mine to edit. I am the one who should move.
try: Find one teaching you quietly resist. Read about it today with an open heart, not to argue.

title: You knew me for a lifetime. Did I ever lie?
subtitle: His forty honest years as evidence
then: Ibn Kathir notes the Prophet ﷺ grew up among them and was never accused of lying. Asked by Heraclius, Abu Sufyan, then his enemy, {reward}admitted he had never lied.{/reward} Heraclius said: {idea}how could a man who does not lie about people lie about Allah?{/idea}
now: Your reputation at work, in the family chat, with your neighbours is being built right now. {reward}Years of small honesty{/reward} become the reason people believe you when it matters most.
old: A small white lie here and there does not affect anything.
new: A lifetime of honesty is itself a kind of proof.
try: Catch one small exaggeration you would normally say today, and say the plain truth instead.

title: Nothing is worse than lying in Allah's name.
subtitle: Inventing lies about Allah, or denying His signs
then: Ibn Kathir says the difference between the Prophet ﷺ and Musaylamah the liar was {idea}clearer than forenoon and midnight.{/idea} When Musaylamah recited his imitation, Amr bin Al-As, not yet Muslim, told him: {trap}you know that I know you are a liar.{/trap}
now: A post goes viral: a quote attributed to the Prophet ﷺ, no source, perfect for your argument. {trap}Sharing it is easy.{/trap} Putting words in Allah's mouth, or His Messenger's, is the heaviest kind of lie.
old: If a religious quote sounds good, it is fine to share it.
new: Speaking for Allah without knowledge is the gravest lie, so I check before I share.
try: Before forwarding any religious quote today, find its source. If you cannot, do not send it.

title: They worship what can neither help nor harm them.
subtitle: Trusting intercessors that have no power
then: The idolators of Makkah worshipped idols, hoping those gods would plead for them before Allah. Ibn Kathir says {trap}these gods own nothing and have no authority over anything.{/trap} The verse asks: {idea}are you informing Allah of something in the heavens or earth He does not know?{/idea}
now: The lucky bracelet before the exam. The ritual before the interview. The person you think knows the right people. {trap}Little helpers you count on more than Allah.{/trap} None of them can move anything without Him.
old: I need something extra between me and Allah to get things done.
new: Nothing I lean on besides Allah can help or harm me on its own.
try: Notice one object or ritual you rely on for luck. Replace it with a short dua today.

title: Humanity started as one, then split apart.
subtitle: Shirk came later, and judgment is delayed
then: Ibn Abbas said there were {reward}ten centuries between Adam and Nuh, all on Islam.{/reward} Then people differed and worshipped idols. Ibn Kathir explains the Word that preceded: {idea}Allah would not punish until proof was established, and gave a respite until a set term.{/idea}
now: Your family once prayed together. Now the cousins barely speak and everyone has their own version. {idea}Division is not the original state.{/idea} The time before judgment is a chance to return, not a sign that nothing matters.
old: If Allah does not settle a dispute now, maybe it does not matter.
new: The delay is mercy and time to return, not indifference.
try: Message one relative you have drifted from. Just a simple greeting.

title: Show us a miracle, they said. Wait, he answered.
subtitle: Demanding signs when the heart is closed
then: Quraysh asked for Mount Safa to turn to gold, or for gardens and rivers in Makkah. Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was given the choice and {reward}chose that their request not be answered{/reward}, since a refused miracle brings swift punishment. {trap}Their asking came from stubbornness, not search.{/trap}
now: "If Allah gets me this job, I will start praying." You set the test, you set the deadline. {trap}It sounds like seeking. Often it is bargaining.{/trap} The signs you already have are usually enough.
old: I will commit once Allah shows me a clear sign.
new: Demanding a sign on my terms can be a way to avoid the signs I already have.
try: Write down three signs of Allah's care you have already seen this year.

title: Mercy arrives after hardship, and they start scheming.
subtitle: How relief can turn into ingratitude
then: After a night of rain, the Prophet ﷺ told his companions that Allah said: {reward}whoever says we had rain by Allah's grace believes in Me{/reward}, and {trap}whoever credits a star believes in the star.{/trap} The verse adds that the angels record every scheme.
now: The bonus came through. The test result was fine. Within an hour you are telling everyone how well you negotiated, how lucky the timing was. {trap}Allah slips out of the story.{/trap}
old: Good things come from my effort and good timing.
new: When relief comes, the first credit belongs to Allah's mercy.
try: The next good news you share today, start with alhamdulillah before any detail.

title: In the storm, every other god disappears.
subtitle: Sincere prayer when the waves close in

row.title: Allah alone
sub: save us, we will be grateful

then: Ibn Kathir says when sailors felt surrounded and about to drown, {idea}they would not call an idol or statue, only Allah.{/idea} They promised: if You save us, we will worship You alone. {trap}The storm stripped away every false hope.{/trap}
now: Turbulence. The seatbelt sign. The plane drops and the cabin goes quiet. In that moment you are not thinking about your stocks or your followers. {idea}You are talking to Allah, and you mean it.{/idea}
old: I rely on many things, and Allah is one of them.
new: When everything else fails, I find out it was only ever Him.
try: Make one dua today with the same sincerity you would have in a storm.

title: Safe on land, they break the promise they made.
subtitle: Your wrongdoing only falls back on you
then: Ibn Kathir says once rescued, they {trap}returned as if they had never faced danger or promised anything.{/trap} The verse warns: your injustice is only against yourselves. He cites the hadith that {trap}oppression and cutting family ties{/trap} are among the sins most likely punished in this world too.
now: You swore in the hospital waiting room you would call your mother every week. She recovered. It has been two months. {idea}The promise did not expire.{/idea} And neglect hurts you most of all.
old: Once the danger passed, the promise was no longer urgent.
new: The promise I made in fear is still owed in safety, and breaking it harms me first.
try: Remember one promise you made to Allah in a hard moment. Keep one part of it today.

title: This life blooms like a field, then is gone overnight.
subtitle: The parable of the green field
then: Ibn Kathir describes farmers looking at their blooming hills, {trap}sure they had full power over the harvest.{/trap} Then a frost or storm dried every leaf. Qatadah said: {idea}as if it had never flourished.{/idea} This world runs from those who chase it.
now: The business finally takes off. The portfolio is up. The house is just how you wanted it. One phone call can flatten it overnight. {idea}Enjoy the field, but do not think you own the weather.{/idea}
old: Once I build it well enough, it is secure.
new: Everything in this life can be gone overnight, so I hold it lightly.
try: Look at the thing you are proudest of building. Say: this is from Allah, and it is His to take.

title: Allah is inviting you to the Home of Peace.
subtitle: The invitation after the fading field
then: Right after the field that vanishes, Allah {reward}invites people to Paradise, the Abode of Peace{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ described a dream: a king builds a house, lays a feast, and sends a messenger to invite people. {idea}Some accepted, some did not.{/idea}
now: Your inbox is full of invitations: sales, events, offers ending tonight. Most vanish by next week. {reward}One invitation has been open your whole life{/reward}, to a home that does not fade.
old: Paradise feels far away and abstract.
new: It is a personal invitation, already sent, waiting for my reply.
try: Make one choice today that you would count as saying yes to that invitation.

title: For those who do good, the best and even more.
subtitle: The reward beyond reward
then: Many early scholars explained the extra as {reward}looking at Allah's Noble Face.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said that when the people of Paradise enter, the veil will be lifted, and {reward}nothing will be dearer to them than looking at Him.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes this comes by grace, not by deeds alone.
now: You help a colleague and expect a thank you at most. You care for an ageing parent and nobody claps. {reward}Allah's answer to good is not just equal. It is more.{/reward}
old: Good deeds are a fair trade, one for one.
new: Allah repays good with the best, and then gives more than I could ask.
try: Do one good deed today hoping only for the extra that Allah adds.

title: Evil is repaid only with its like, never more.
subtitle: Justice for those who earned bad deeds
then: After the generous reward, Ibn Kathir notes {idea}Allah's justice with the wrongdoers: evil repaid with its like, without any increase.{/idea} Yet with no protector, {trap}their faces will be dark and covered with disgrace.{/trap}
now: One harsh word in a meeting. You replay it for weeks and decide you are a terrible person. {idea}Allah weighs evil exactly, and good with extra.{/idea} The scale leans toward hope, if you keep adding good.
old: My mistakes outweigh everything good I do.
new: Evil counts as one, good counts as more, so I keep adding good.
try: After your next mistake today, follow it straight away with one good deed.

title: On that Day, the idols will deny their worshippers.
subtitle: When false partners walk away
then: Ibn Kathir describes all creation gathered, then {trap}the idolators separated from the believers{/trap} and told to stay in place with what they worshipped. Those false partners {trap}deny any part in it{/trap}, as in other verses where the followed disown their followers.
now: The boss you bent your values for. The crowd whose approval you chased. The brand you built your identity on. {trap}Ask them to stand with you on the Day.{/trap} Only what you did for Allah stays loyal.
old: The people and things I please will have my back.
new: Anything I put in Allah's place will walk away from me when I need it.
try: Name one approval you chase more than Allah's. Do one thing today for His pleasure alone.

title: We never knew you worshipped us, the idols say.
subtitle: Allah as witness to the denial
then: Continuing the scene of the Day, Ibn Kathir explains the false partners' reply: {trap}we never called you to worship us, never ordered it, never accepted it.{/trap} They call on {idea}Allah as sufficient witness{/idea} between them and those who worshipped them.
now: You refresh the celebrity's page, defend them in comment threads, model your life on theirs. {trap}They have no idea you exist.{/trap} Devotion poured into something that cannot know you is devotion lost.
old: The things I devote myself to know and value me back.
new: Only Allah truly knows my devotion. Everything else is unaware of me.
try: Count the hours you gave today to something that does not know you. Give ten minutes to Allah instead.

title: Every soul faces exactly what it sent ahead.
subtitle: The return to the true Master
then: Ibn Kathir says on that Day {idea}every soul shall know all it had sent forth, good and evil.{/idea} He cites: read your book, you are enough as a reckoner against yourself. And {trap}everything they invented to worship besides Allah simply disappears.{/trap}
now: Your screen time report arrives on Sunday. Every hour accounted for, no excuses attached. {idea}Imagine that report for every deed.{/idea} The good news: you are still writing it.
old: Most of what I do just disappears.
new: Everything I do is sent ahead, and I will meet it again.
try: Tonight, look back at your day and name one deed you would like to meet again.

title: Who feeds you, gives you sight, and runs everything?
subtitle: Questions whose answer they already knew
then: The Makkans admitted Allah was Creator and Provider. Ibn Kathir explains this {idea}admission was itself the evidence against them{/idea}: if He alone provides, controls sight and hearing, and governs everything, {trap}why worship anything else?{/trap}
now: Your eyes reading this. Your ears hearing the kettle. The salary that landed this month. {idea}You know who gave them.{/idea} The question is whether your day looks like you know.
old: I believe Allah gives me everything. That is enough.
new: Knowing He gives me everything should change how I live, not just what I say.
try: Close your eyes for ten seconds, then open them and thank Allah for your sight.

title: After the truth, what is left except error?
subtitle: There is no middle ground beyond the truth
then: Having made them admit Allah does all of this, the verse concludes: {idea}that is Allah, your Lord in truth.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says anything worshipped besides Him {trap}is false.{/trap} So how can you turn away from Him knowing He made and governs everything?
now: You know which choice is right. You still look for a version where you can keep both. {trap}The comfortable maybe.{/trap} The verse says once the truth is clear, what is left over is not a middle path.
old: I can stay undecided and that is neutral.
new: Once I know the truth, turning from it is not neutral, it is drifting into error.
try: Pick one thing you know is right and keep sitting on the fence about. Choose today.

title: Persistent defiance closes the door to belief.
subtitle: When the word of Allah comes true on the rebellious
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the idolators {trap}knew Allah was Creator and Sustainer, yet persisted{/trap} in worshipping others. Because they kept at it, {trap}the Word of Allah proved true against them.{/trap} The issue was not one slip but stubborn persistence.
now: The first time you ignore your conscience, it nags. The tenth time, it whispers. The hundredth, it is quiet. {idea}Persistence shapes the heart.{/idea} The good news: turning back also becomes easier each time.
old: I can keep ignoring this, and turn around whenever I like.
new: Each time I persist against what I know, turning back gets harder.
try: Act on one quiet nudge of conscience today before it fades.

title: Can any of your partners start creation and repeat it?
subtitle: Only Allah begins and returns creation
then: Ibn Kathir asks with the verse: {idea}who started the heavens and earth, placed the stars, and can repeat it all?{/idea} Only Allah, alone. {trap}So how are you deluded away from the truth?{/trap}
now: You give your phone the first look in the morning and the last at night. It cannot make a single cell. {idea}The One who made you, and will remake you,{/idea} often gets what is left.
old: I give my attention to what feels most useful.
new: The One who creates and recreates deserves my first attention.
try: Tomorrow morning, say a short dhikr before you touch your phone.

title: Follow the guide, not one who needs guiding.
subtitle: Who is worthy to be followed
then: Ibn Kathir asks: will a servant {idea}follow the One who guides to the truth so he may see after blindness{/idea}, or one who {trap}leads only to blindness{/trap}? He recalls Ibrahim asking his father why he worshipped what cannot hear or see.
now: The influencer who has no idea where their own life is going is telling you how to live yours. {trap}A guide who needs a guide.{/trap} Before you follow anyone, ask where they are heading.
old: I follow whoever seems confident.
new: I follow the One who actually knows the way.
try: Unfollow one account today that pulls you away from Allah.

title: Guesswork is no match for the truth.
subtitle: Following assumption instead of evidence
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}did not follow their religion out of evidence and proof, but mere conjecture and imagination.{/trap} And {idea}conjecture is no substitute for the truth.{/idea} Allah knows what they do.
now: "I heard that..." "Someone said..." You form a strong opinion about a person, a ruling, a news story, from a screenshot. {trap}Assumption feels like knowledge until the facts arrive.{/trap}
old: My strong feeling about it is good enough.
new: A guess, however confident, cannot stand against the truth.
try: Before stating one strong opinion today, ask yourself: how do I actually know this?

title: No one but Allah could have produced this Quran.
subtitle: It confirms what came before and explains it
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}the eloquence, clarity, and precision of the Quran cannot be but from Allah.{/idea} The Arabs prized poetry above all arts, yet {reward}those who believed did so because of what they felt in its beauty and benefit.{/reward}
now: You hear a recitation in a car park and it stops you mid-step. You do not know every word, but something in it lands. {idea}That feeling has a source.{/idea} Many have believed because of it.
old: The Quran is a religious text like any other.
new: Its words carry a mark no human speech carries.
try: Listen to one short surah today with full attention, eyes closed.

title: He made it up? Then bring one surah like it.
subtitle: The open challenge to produce a single chapter
then: Ibn Kathir explains the challenge came in stages: {idea}first the whole Quran, then ten surahs, then just one.{/idea} The people of Makkah were masters of poetry. {trap}Still, none could answer it.{/trap}
now: Someone online says the Quran is just borrowed ideas. You feel a flicker of doubt. {idea}The challenge is still open, centuries later.{/idea} Doubt can be the start of looking closer, not the end.
old: When someone attacks the Quran, I feel defenceless.
new: The Quran has stood its own challenge for centuries. I can study it calmly.
try: Read the meaning of one short surah today, slowly, line by line.

title: They rejected what they never understood.
subtitle: Denying before knowing
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}did not believe in the Quran and had not yet grasped or comprehended it.{/trap} They belied it out of ignorance, just as past nations did. {idea}Look at how those nations ended.{/idea}
now: You dismiss a lecture after the first minute. You reject an idea because of who said it, not what it says. {trap}Rejecting before understanding{/trap} feels like confidence. It is often just not listening.
old: I already know enough to judge it.
new: Before I reject something, I owe it real understanding.
try: Read one thing you disagree with today all the way to the end before forming a view.

title: Some will believe, some will not. Allah knows who.
subtitle: Leaving outcomes to the One who knows
then: Ibn Kathir says among those the Prophet ﷺ was sent to, {reward}some would believe, follow, and benefit{/reward}, and {trap}some would die refusing.{/trap} Allah knows best who deserves guidance.
now: You share something beneficial in the family group chat. One cousin replies with a heart, another with an eye-roll emoji. {idea}Your job was to share it kindly.{/idea} What happens next is not in your hands.
old: If they do not accept it, I failed.
new: I convey with kindness. Who accepts is known to Allah.
try: Share one beneficial thing with someone today, and let go of how they react.

title: My deeds are mine, and yours are yours.
subtitle: A calm reply to being rejected
then: When the idolators rejected him, the Prophet ﷺ was told to say: {idea}for me are my deeds and for you are yours.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to Surah Al-Kafirun and to Ibrahim telling his people {idea}we are free of what you worship.{/idea}
now: The argument in the comments has gone forty replies deep. You keep typing. {idea}You can stop.{/idea} Say what is true once, then step away. Your record is your own, and so is theirs.
old: If they reject me, I have to keep arguing until I win.
new: I can be clear, then let each of us carry our own deeds.
try: Leave one argument today, online or offline, with a calm last sentence.

title: They hear your words, but can you make the deaf hear?
subtitle: Listening is not the same as hearing
then: Ibn Kathir says some listened to the Prophet ﷺ, his beautiful speech and the Quran. {idea}But guiding people to the truth was not up to him or them.{/idea} {trap}You cannot make the deaf hear{/trap}, except if Allah wills.
now: You have explained it to your brother five times, each time better. He nods and changes nothing. {idea}It is not your eloquence that opens hearts.{/idea} Keep being kind, and make dua for him.
old: If I find the perfect words, they will change.
new: I do my part. Opening hearts belongs to Allah.
try: Make one dua today for someone you have been trying to convince.

title: They look at you, but some eyes do not see.
subtitle: Seeing the Prophet ﷺ without seeing the truth
then: Ibn Kathir says people looked at the Prophet ﷺ, his dignity and great conduct, {idea}clear evidence for those with insight.{/idea} Believers looked with respect, while {trap}deniers looked with contempt and mockery.{/trap} The same sight, two results.
now: Two people watch the same video of someone praying in the rain. One feels moved. The other scrolls past with a smirk. {idea}What you see depends on the heart behind your eyes.{/idea}
old: If something is true, I will see it straight away.
new: Seeing truth needs an open heart, not just open eyes.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to let you see the truth as truth.

title: Allah wrongs no one. People wrong themselves.
subtitle: Where the harm really comes from
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith qudsi in Muslim: {idea}O My servants, I have forbidden oppression for Myself.{/idea} And at its end: {trap}whoever finds other than good, let him blame no one but himself.{/trap}
now: You stayed up until 3 a.m., missed Fajr, and blamed the alarm. You snapped at your partner and blamed the stress. {idea}Owning your part is not self-hatred.{/idea} It is where change starts.
old: Bad things happen to me because life is unfair.
new: Allah is never unjust. Often the harm I feel is harm I did to myself.
try: Name one problem today where your own choice played a part. Fix one small piece of it.

title: A whole lifetime will feel like one hour.
subtitle: The shortness of this life seen from the Gathering

row.title: they know each other
sub: but each is busy with himself

then: Ibn Kathir gathers verses where people say {trap}we stayed only an hour, or a day, or part of a day.{/trap} They will recognise their families, yet {idea}everyone will be busy with himself.{/idea} The greatest loss is to be cut off from loved ones on that Day.
now: Your school years already feel like a blur. The last decade went by in what seems like a few months. {idea}Now picture the whole life seen from the end.{/idea} One hour. What do you want that hour to have held?
old: I have plenty of time to get serious later.
new: My whole life will feel like an hour, so this hour matters.
try: Spend one hour today on something you would be glad to have done when looking back.

title: Whether you see the outcome or not, Allah is witness.
subtitle: Results are His, in this life or the next
then: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}We may show you some of what We promised them in your lifetime{/idea}, or take you first. Either way, their return is to Allah, and {reward}He is Witness over what they did.{/reward}
now: The colleague who stole your idea and never paid for it. The relative who wronged you and seems fine. {idea}You may never see the account settled.{/idea} You do not have to. Allah saw it.
old: If I never see justice done, it never will be.
new: Allah witnessed it. Justice is certain whether I see it or not.
try: Hand one old injustice to Allah in dua today, and let yourself put it down.

title: Every nation had a messenger, and judgment is fair.
subtitle: Each community judged in the presence of its messenger

row.title: first
sub: by honor of its Messenger ﷺ

then: Mujahid said this is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Kathir says each nation will stand with {idea}its Messenger and the book of its deeds.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}we are the last, and the first to be judged on the Day.{/reward}
now: You belong to the nation that will be called first. That is an honor, and it comes with a question. {idea}What would your page say if it were read out today?{/idea}
old: Judgment is something far away and vague.
new: My community will stand first, with its Messenger ﷺ. I want my page to honor him.
try: Do one sunnah today that you usually skip, out of love for the Prophet ﷺ.

title: So when is it coming, they mocked.
subtitle: Asking for the date instead of preparing

row.title: believers
sub: fear it, know it is true

then: Ibn Kathir says the idolators {trap}demanded the punishment be hastened{/trap}, asking about its time, though the answer would not benefit them. He cites a verse: {reward}those who believe are fearful of it, and know it is the truth.{/reward}
now: "Everyone keeps saying life is short. I am 25. Relax." You ask when, as if a date would change anything. {idea}The question that helps is not when, but how ready.{/idea}
old: Until I know when, I do not need to worry about it.
new: Knowing it is certain is enough to start preparing.
try: Write one sentence: if my life ended this week, what would I want to have fixed?

title: Not even the Prophet ﷺ controls his own harm or benefit.
subtitle: Every term is fixed, neither delayed nor advanced
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to say: {idea}I have no power over harm or benefit for myself except what Allah wills.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains he was told the Hour would come but not when. {trap}When a term arrives, it cannot be delayed or advanced a moment.{/trap}
now: You plan to visit your grandmother next month, when work calms down. You plan to start praying properly after the move. {trap}Your appointment with Allah is not on your calendar.{/trap}
old: I will have time to do it later.
new: My term is set, and I cannot move it by one hour.
try: Do today one thing you keep pushing to later: a visit, a call, a prayer.

title: Which part of a sudden punishment would you rush?
subtitle: Impatience for what no one could bear
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah told His Messenger ﷺ to warn that {trap}His punishment would come suddenly, by night or by day.{/trap} The question exposes the dare: {idea}which part of it would anyone really want hurried?{/idea}
now: "If it is so bad, let it happen then." You hear it said about health warnings, debt, a marriage in trouble. {trap}Daring the consequence feels brave.{/trap} Nobody wants it once it arrives.
old: Daring the warning shows I am not afraid.
new: Rushing a consequence I could not bear is not courage.
try: Take one warning in your life seriously today, and take one small step to heed it.

title: Believing only when it lands is too late.
subtitle: Faith that comes after the punishment
then: Ibn Kathir cites the verse where they cry: {trap}Our Lord, we have now seen and heard.{/trap} And another: {trap}when they saw Our punishment they said, we believe.{/trap} But {idea}their faith could not help them once they saw it.{/idea}
now: You meant to start saving. The car breaks, the rent is due, and now you are motivated. {idea}Some doors only open before the crisis.{/idea} The door of repentance is open today.
old: I will turn to Allah once things get serious.
new: Faith that waits until the end may come too late. It is worth most right now.
try: Make a sincere tawbah today for one thing, without waiting for a crisis.

title: You are repaid only for what you earned.
subtitle: The lasting outcome of wrongdoing
then: Ibn Kathir says this will be said on the Day, {trap}as blame and rebuke.{/trap} He cites the verse: {idea}you are only being repaid for what you used to do.{/idea} The verse ends with a question that answers itself.
now: Every day you put something into your account: words, habits, kindness, neglect. {idea}What comes out is what went in.{/idea} The deposit window is still open.
old: What happens at the end has nothing to do with today.
new: The ending is the sum of what I earn every day.
try: Add one clear good deposit today: charity, a kind word, or a prayer on time.

title: Is it really true? Yes, by my Lord, it is.
subtitle: An oath that the Resurrection is real

row.title: He made you from nothing
sub: He says Be, and it is

then: They asked whether rising from the graves, after bodies become sand, was true. The Prophet ﷺ was told to swear by his Lord. Ibn Kathir notes {idea}only two other verses carry this oath{/idea}, and that {idea}the One who made you from nothing can bring you back.{/idea}
now: Late at night, the doubt slips in: is any of this real? {idea}The answer comes with an oath.{/idea} Doubt is human. You can bring it to Allah and keep walking.
old: Sometimes I wonder if the afterlife is really real.
new: The Prophet ﷺ answered that question with an oath by his Lord.
try: When doubt visits today, say: yes, by my Lord, it is the truth.

title: They would give the whole earth to escape it.
subtitle: Regret that no ransom can buy away
then: Ibn Kathir says when Resurrection comes, wrongdoers {trap}will wish to ransom themselves with the weight of the earth in gold.{/trap} They hide their regret when they see the punishment. And still {idea}they will be judged with justice.{/idea}
now: Money gets you out of a parking ticket, a late fee, a long queue. You start to believe it can get you out of anything. {idea}One day it will not.{/idea} Spend it now on what will count then.
old: With enough money I can get out of most trouble.
new: On that Day the whole earth would not buy one escape, but charity today does count.
try: Give a small amount in charity today, as an investment in what lasts.

title: Everything belongs to Allah, and His promise is true.
subtitle: Ownership and a promise most people forget
then: After the scene of regret, the verse opens with a call to attention: {idea}all in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says {reward}His promise is true and will be fulfilled.{/reward} Yet most people live without knowing it.
now: Your name is on the lease, the car title, the bank card. It feels like ownership. {idea}It is a loan with your name on it.{/idea} The real Owner has promised to come back to every account.
old: What is in my name is mine.
new: Everything belongs to Allah. I am holding it for a while.
try: Pick one thing you own and use it today in a way the Owner would love.

title: He gives life, He takes it, and you go back to Him.
subtitle: The whole story of a life in one line
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}He gives life and causes death, and to Him is everyone's return.{/idea} He knows {idea}where every speck of a body has gone{/idea}, on land or in the sea. Nothing is lost to Him.
now: A birth announcement and a funeral notice in the same family group chat, the same week. {idea}Both come from the same Hand.{/idea} And both point to the same return.
old: Birth and death are just things that happen.
new: Life and death are both from Allah, and both lead back to Him.
try: Make a dua today for someone who has passed away, and for one baby born recently.

title: Advice, healing, guidance, and mercy, all in one Book.
subtitle: What the Quran does for the heart

key.label: What the Quran is for you

then: Ibn Kathir calls this {reward}a great favor{/reward} on all people. The Quran is a warning that shields from shameful deeds, and {reward}a cure from suspicion and doubts{/reward} that cleans the heart. Its guidance and mercy reach {idea}those who believe in it firmly.{/idea}
now: Your chest feels tight after a bad day. You reach for a show, a snack, a scroll. {reward}There is a healing written for what is in your chest.{/reward} It works best when you actually open it.
old: The Quran is for rules. For my feelings I need something else.
new: The Quran was sent as healing for what is inside my chest.
try: Next time you feel heavy today, read five verses slowly before anything else.

title: Rejoice in His bounty and mercy, not in your savings.
subtitle: What is truly worth celebrating
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}let them rejoice in the guidance and the religion of truth{/reward}. It is better than anything people gather {trap}from a world whose bloom is vanishing.{/trap}
now: You post the promotion, the new phone, the holiday photos. When did you last feel that same joy about having faith at all? {reward}That is the bigger win.{/reward}
old: I celebrate what I achieve and buy.
new: Being guided by Allah is the gift most worth celebrating.
try: Tell someone today, or tell Allah, one thing about your faith you are glad of.

title: Who gave you the right to forbid what Allah allowed?
subtitle: Making up lawful and unlawful by desire
then: Ibn Abbas and others said this criticised the idolators who {trap}cut the ears of their camels and declared them forbidden{/trap} for themselves. The Prophet ﷺ told one man: {reward}what Allah has given you is lawful.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says their rules came from {trap}desires and false opinions, not evidence.{/trap}
now: Someone in the family declares a thing haram with total confidence. Another calls something fine because everyone does it. {idea}Both are claims about Allah.{/idea} The verse asks: did He say so, or did we?
old: If it feels wrong or right to me, that settles it.
new: Only Allah makes things lawful or unlawful. My feelings do not.
try: Next time you are about to say this is haram or halal, pause and ask: do I actually know?

title: Allah is generous, yet most people are not grateful.
subtitle: A warning to inventors and a reminder of bounty
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah's grace is in {reward}the many good things He made permissible{/reward}, and He forbade only what harms. Yet many {trap}prohibited what Allah gave them, and made life hard and narrow for themselves.{/trap}
now: You picture faith as a list of no. Look at your plate, your bed, your family, your work. {reward}Most of life is wide open and blessed.{/reward} The few limits are there to protect you.
old: Religion is mostly about what I cannot have.
new: Allah made most things good and lawful. The limits are mercy too.
try: List five lawful blessings you enjoyed today, and thank Allah for each.

title: Whatever you are doing right now, He is watching.
subtitle: Nothing, not even a speck, is hidden from Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}nothing escapes Allah's knowledge, not even the weight of a speck of dust.{/idea} If He knows every leaf and grain, what of those commanded to worship Him? He cites the Prophet ﷺ on ihsan: {reward}worship Allah as if you see Him, and if not, know He sees you.{/reward}
now: Alone in the office after everyone leaves. Late at night with the phone. Washing dishes no one will thank you for. {reward}Allah is there for all of it.{/reward} That can be a warning, and also deep comfort.
old: What I do when no one is around is my own business.
new: Allah is witness to every moment, so every moment can be worship.
try: Do one ordinary task today slowly, remembering that Allah is watching you do it.

title: The friends of Allah will have no fear and no grief.
subtitle: Who the awliya of Allah are
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}every pious, God-fearing person is a friend of Allah.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ described people who {reward}loved one another for Allah's sake, without money or kinship{/reward}, on platforms of light, with no fear when others fear.
now: Your friend from the mosque who checks on you when you go quiet. Not family, no deal between you. {reward}Love like that, for Allah's sake,{/reward} is one road to being among His friends.
old: Friends of Allah are a special few, not ordinary people.
new: Any believer who is mindful of Allah can be His friend.
try: Message one friend today simply to say you love them for the sake of Allah.

title: Two things make a friend of Allah: faith and mindfulness.
subtitle: The definition is short and open to all
then: The previous verse named the friends of Allah. This one defines them. Ibn Kathir says Allah's friends are {idea}those who believe and have taqwa, as He defined them.{/idea} No lineage, wealth, or wonders are required.
now: You are not a scholar, you have no religious title, you miss things often. {idea}The bar is not fame. It is faith and staying mindful.{/idea} That you can work on today, in the supermarket queue.
old: I am too ordinary to be close to Allah.
new: Faith plus mindfulness is the whole definition, and it is open to me.
try: Pick one moment today where you would normally be careless, and be mindful of Allah instead.

title: Good news for them, here and in the Hereafter.
subtitle: Glad tidings that start in this life
then: Asked about the good news in this world, the Prophet ﷺ said {reward}it is the good dream a servant sees, or that is seen about him.{/reward} When a man is praised for his good deeds, he called it {reward}good news hastened for the believer.{/reward} Others said it is the angels' greeting at death.
now: A good dream that leaves you calm all morning. A stranger thanking you for something you forgot you did. {reward}Small glad tidings, sent early.{/reward} Notice them.
old: Reward for faith only comes after I die.
new: Allah sends glimpses of good news already, in this life.
try: Tonight, remember one recent good sign in your life and thank Allah for it.

title: Do not let their words get to you. Honor is Allah's.
subtitle: When mockery hurts
then: Allah told His Messenger ﷺ not to grieve over the idolators' remarks, but to {idea}rely on Allah, ask His help, and trust Him.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says {reward}all might and honor belong to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.{/reward}
now: Someone laughs at your hijab, your beard, your prayer break at work. It replays in your head all evening. {reward}Your honor was never theirs to give or take.{/reward} Allah heard every word.
old: When people mock me, I lose something.
new: My honor comes from Allah. Their words cannot reach it.
try: Next time a comment stings today, say quietly: Allah hears, Allah knows.

title: Everyone belongs to Allah. Partners are only guesswork.
subtitle: Following false partners is following a lie
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolators worshipped idols that {trap}own nothing and can neither harm nor benefit.{/trap} They had no evidence, and followed only {trap}their own conjecture and lies.{/trap} Everyone in the heavens and earth already belongs to Allah.
now: "If I do not do it this way, my career is over." "Without them, I am nothing." You give powers to people and plans that were never theirs. {idea}They belong to Allah, just like you.{/idea}
old: Some people hold my future in their hands.
new: Everyone I fear or rely on belongs to Allah, just like me.
try: Name one person you fear too much. Remind yourself today that they too belong to Allah.

title: Night for rest, day for seeing. That is a sign.
subtitle: The daily rhythm as a gift to listen to
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah made {reward}the night for His servants to rest from weariness{/reward}, and the day {reward}bright to seek a living and meet their needs.{/reward} These are signs for {idea}people who hear and take a lesson.{/idea}
now: It is 1 a.m. and you are still scrolling in bed, the phone lighting your face. Tomorrow you will drag through the morning. {reward}The night was made as a gift of rest.{/reward} Accept it.
old: Night is just more time for me to use.
new: Night was made for rest. Using it that way is gratitude.
try: Put your phone away thirty minutes earlier tonight and sleep with a short dhikr.

title: Allah needs nothing. He has no need of a son.
subtitle: Saying about Allah what you do not know
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is {idea}Self-Sufficient, free of any need, while everything else desperately needs Him.{/idea} Everything belongs to Him, so how could He have a son from His own creation? {trap}You have no proof. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?{/trap}
now: "Allah would not mind." "God just wants me to be happy." You say confident things about Allah in conversation that you never checked. {trap}Speaking about Him without knowledge is serious.{/trap} Learn first, then speak.
old: I can describe Allah however makes sense to me.
new: Allah needs nothing. I should speak of Him only with knowledge.
try: Learn the meaning of one of Allah's names today from a reliable source.

title: Lying about Allah never leads to success.
subtitle: No real prosperity for those who fabricate
then: Ibn Kathir says those who fabricate about Allah {trap}will never prosper, in this world or the Hereafter.{/trap} {idea}Allah gives them respite and leads them step by step{/idea}, so their apparent comfort is not the success it seems.
now: Someone builds a large following by saying whatever about religion gets the most views. Money, fame, applause. {trap}It looks like winning.{/trap} The verse defines success differently.
old: If it brings attention and money, it worked.
new: Real success never comes from lying about Allah, however good it looks.
try: Before sharing any religious claim today, check it is true. Honesty about Allah is success.

title: A little enjoyment, then the return to Allah.
subtitle: How short the comfort of falsehood is
then: Ibn Kathir explains this as {trap}only a short period{/trap} of enjoyment in this world. Then comes the return on the Day of Resurrection, and {trap}the outcome of their denial and lies about Allah.{/trap}
now: The thrill of a choice you know is wrong lasts an evening. The regret lasts much longer. {idea}Every pleasure built on a lie is brief.{/idea} The return is long.
old: The pleasure now is worth whatever comes later.
new: Enjoyment built on falsehood is brief, and the return to Allah is certain.
try: Turn down one small pleasure today that you know is not right, and feel the difference.

title: Nuh said: do your worst. I rely on Allah.
subtitle: Calm courage under pressure
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to recite Nuh's story to Quraysh as a lesson. Ibn Kathir explains Nuh's words: {idea}if my preaching offends you, I do not care, and I will not stop.{/idea} {trap}Plot with all your idols and give me no respite.{/trap} He feared them not, because they stood on nothing.
now: Your whole team mocks the way you refuse to fudge the numbers. The pressure in the room is heavy. {idea}Nuh stood alone against a nation, calm.{/idea} You can stand in one meeting.
old: If everyone pushes against me, I have to give in.
new: When I rely on Allah, their pressure has nothing to stand on.
try: Hold to one right thing today that others pressure you to drop. Say bismillah first.

title: I never asked you for payment. My reward is Allah's.
subtitle: Advice given with no strings attached
then: Nuh said: {idea}I have not asked you anything for my advice. My reward is from Allah, and I am commanded to be a Muslim.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says {reward}Islam is the religion of all the prophets, first to last{/reward}; their laws differ, their religion is one.
now: You help a friend move house, fix a relative's CV, give honest advice. Part of you waits for the favour back. {reward}Nuh asked nothing, for centuries.{/reward} The reward was already arranged.
old: When I help, I expect something in return.
new: My reward is with Allah, so I can give advice and help freely.
try: Help someone today and tell no one, expecting nothing back.

title: The ark saved the few, the flood took the deniers.
subtitle: How Nuh's story ended
then: They denied Nuh, and Allah {reward}delivered him and those on his religion in the ark{/reward}, making them successors on the earth. {trap}Those who belied the signs were drowned.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says the message to the Prophet ﷺ was: see how We saved the believers.
now: You are the only one in your friend group who does not drink, or the only one at work who prays. It feels like being on a tiny boat. {reward}Allah saved the small boat.{/reward}
old: If I am in the minority, I must be wrong.
new: Being one of the few with Allah is safer than being one of the many without Him.
try: Thank Allah today for one person who shares your boat, and tell them you appreciate them.

title: Rejecting from the start seals the heart.
subtitle: When early refusal becomes a lock
then: After Nuh, messengers came to their peoples with clear proofs. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they would not believe because they had rejected it from the beginning.{/trap} He calls it {trap}a serious warning{/trap} to the Makkans who rejected the last Messenger ﷺ.
now: You decided years ago that a certain relative is always wrong. Now even when they say something wise, you cannot hear it. {trap}An early no hardens into a lock.{/trap} Keep the door open.
old: Once I have decided, nothing needs revisiting.
new: Rejecting before listening can seal my own heart.
try: Revisit one opinion you formed long ago. Ask Allah to show you the truth about it.

title: Musa and Harun came with signs, and met arrogance.
subtitle: Too proud to follow the truth
then: After those messengers, Allah sent Musa and Harun to Firaun and his chiefs with proofs. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they were too arrogant to follow the truth and submit to it.{/trap} The story is told to the Makkans, who also had power and pride.
now: Your younger colleague points out your mistake, politely and correctly. The hardest part is not the fix. {trap}It is swallowing your pride.{/trap} Arrogance blocks truth faster than doubt does.
old: I reject it because I am not convinced.
new: Sometimes the real block is pride, not lack of proof.
try: Accept one correction today from someone you would normally dismiss, and thank them.

title: Truth arrived, and they called it obvious magic.
subtitle: Labelling what they knew was true
then: Ibn Kathir says they spoke {trap}as if giving an oath{/trap}, but knew they were lying. He cites the verse: {trap}they denied them wrongfully and arrogantly, though they themselves were convinced.{/trap}
now: You know your friend was right in the argument. Instead you say, "Whatever, you always twist things." {trap}A label is easier than admitting it.{/trap} The truth does not change because you renamed it.
old: If I give it a dismissive name, I do not have to deal with it.
new: Labelling the truth does not change it. It only keeps me from it.
try: Admit one thing today you knew was true but kept brushing off.

title: Is this magic? Magicians never succeed.
subtitle: Musa's question to those who called truth a trick
then: Musa criticised them: {idea}do you say this about the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic?{/idea} He gave the test himself: {trap}magicians will never succeed.{/trap} Illusion fades. Truth stays.
now: The get-rich-quick scheme, the miracle diet, the viral life hack. They dazzle for a month. {idea}Check what is still standing a year later.{/idea} Truth has staying power. Tricks do not.
old: If it impresses me, it is probably real.
new: The real test is what lasts. Tricks never succeed in the end.
try: Think of one flashy promise you are tempted by. Ask: will this still stand in a year?

title: You want to pull us from our fathers' ways.
subtitle: Tradition and fear of losing power

row.title: what is true
sub: even if it is new to us

then: Firaun's chiefs said: {trap}have you come to turn us from what we found our fathers following, so you two can have greatness in the land?{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains greatness here as {trap}grandeur and leadership.{/trap} They feared losing both tradition and status.
now: "We have always done the wedding this way." "In our family we do not talk about that." Some traditions are beautiful. {trap}Some are just habits protecting someone's position.{/trap} Ask which one you are defending.
old: If my family always did it, it must be right.
new: I keep the good of my heritage, but truth outranks habit.
try: Pick one family habit and ask honestly: is this from Allah, or just from us?

title: Firaun summoned every skilled magician to beat the truth.
subtitle: Assembling experts against a clear sign
then: Ibn Kathir says Firaun {trap}wanted to deceive the people with the magicians' tricks{/trap} against the plain truth Musa brought. {reward}The result was the exact opposite.{/reward} In that public festival, the signs of the Lord prevailed.
now: You line up arguments, articles, and clever friends to win a point you know is weak. {trap}Expert help does not turn falsehood into truth.{/trap} Sometimes it backfires completely.
old: With enough experts on my side, I can win any argument.
new: No gathering of experts can defeat a clear truth from Allah.
try: Drop one argument today you are only defending to win.

title: Musa let them go first. Throw what you will.
subtitle: Letting falsehood show itself before the truth
then: The magicians lined up, promised closeness to Firaun and a big reward. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Musa wanted them to begin, so people would see what they made, and then the truth would triumph over it.{/idea} When their spells dazzled the crowd, {trap}Musa felt fear{/trap}, and Allah told him: fear not.
now: In a heated family discussion, you let the other person say everything first, without interrupting. {idea}Calm is a kind of confidence.{/idea} Truth does not need to shout first.
old: I must jump in first, or I will lose.
new: When I am on the side of truth, I can let others speak first.
try: In your next disagreement today, let the other person finish completely before you reply.

title: It is only magic, and Allah will undo it.
subtitle: Allah does not make corrupt work succeed
then: After the magicians cast, Musa said: {trap}what you have brought is sorcery.{/trap} {idea}Allah will make it of no effect. Allah does not set right the work of evildoers.{/idea} His staff swallowed what they made.
now: A shortcut at work: a padded invoice, a hidden flaw in the report. It seems to hold. {idea}Allah does not bless corrupt work.{/idea} Sooner or later it unravels.
old: If no one catches it, the shortcut worked.
new: Allah does not set right corrupt work, so it never truly works.
try: Fix one small dishonest shortcut in your work or habits today.

title: Allah makes the truth stand, whoever hates it.
subtitle: Truth established by His words
then: Musa finished: {idea}Allah will establish the truth by His words, however much the criminals hate it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes that the magicians then {reward}fell down in prostration, saying we believe in the Lord of all that exists.{/reward}
now: You told the truth at work and someone powerful did not like it. The room went cold. {idea}Truth does not need everyone to like it.{/idea} Allah is the One who makes it stand.
old: If the powerful dislike the truth, it will be buried.
new: Allah establishes the truth, however much anyone hates it.
try: Say one true thing today kindly, even if you expect it will not be liked.

title: Only a few young people believed, despite the fear.
subtitle: Faith under a tyrant's shadow
then: Despite all the signs, {reward}only a few offspring of Firaun's people believed{/reward}, among them Firaun's wife and the believer who hid his faith. They feared {trap}Firaun would force them back.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says Firaun was {trap}an evil tyrant and extremely arrogant.{/trap}
now: You are the first in your family to start praying regularly. You are nervous about the jokes at dinner. {reward}Faith does not wait for fear to leave.{/reward} The young believers had more to lose, and still believed.
old: I will take faith seriously once it is easy and safe.
new: Faith can begin even while I am afraid.
try: Do one act of faith today that you have been too shy to do in front of others.

title: If you believe in Allah, then rely on Him.
subtitle: Faith shows itself in trust
then: Musa told the Children of Israel, under Firaun's pressure, to {reward}put their trust in Allah.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah is sufficient for those who trust Him{/idea}, and notes how often worship and reliance appear together, as in {idea}You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help.{/idea}
now: The redundancy email. The test results pending. You pray, and then lie awake running every bad scenario. {reward}Faith includes letting Him carry it.{/reward} You say it in every prayer: You alone we ask for help.
old: I believe in Allah, but I still have to carry everything myself.
new: Believing in Allah means trusting Him with what I cannot carry.
try: In your next prayer, say iyyaka nasta'in slowly, and hand Him one specific worry.

title: On Allah we rely. Do not make us a trial for oppressors.
subtitle: A dua for the weak under pressure
then: The Children of Israel answered Musa: {reward}in Allah we put our trust.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains their dua: {trap}do not give them victory over us, so they think they were right and we were wrong.{/trap} Mujahid said it means do not let them push us into trial.
now: You are being treated unfairly by a manager or landlord. You worry about the harm, and also about what it does to your faith. {reward}This dua covers both.{/reward} Trust Allah, and ask Him to keep you steady.
old: When I am oppressed, my only worry is the harm.
new: I also ask Allah to protect my faith from being shaken by it.
try: Learn this dua today: Rabbana la taj'alna fitnatan lil-qawmi az-zalimin.

title: Save us by Your mercy, not by our strength.
subtitle: The second half of their dua
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}save us through Your mercy and beneficence{/reward} from those who denied the truth. Their dua ends with a statement of trust: {idea}we truly have believed in You and put our trust in You.{/idea}
now: You have no connections, no savings cushion, no backup plan. It feels like powerlessness. {reward}Mercy is not earned by strength.{/reward} Ask for it plainly, as they did.
old: Without power or resources, I have no way out.
new: Allah's mercy can save me where my strength cannot.
try: Make a short dua today that begins: O Allah, by Your mercy, save me from...

title: When the streets are unsafe, make your home a place of prayer.
subtitle: Turning houses into places of worship

row.title: at home too
sub: the house as a prayer place

then: Ibn Abbas said the Children of Israel told Musa they {trap}could not pray in public before Firaun's people.{/trap} So {idea}Allah let them pray in their houses, built facing the qiblah.{/idea} Mujahid said they feared being killed at their gatherings, so prayer could be in secret.
now: Your home is where you scroll, eat, work, and argue. {idea}Does it have a corner where you pray?{/idea} A rug by the window, facing qiblah, can turn a flat into a place of worship.
old: Home is for rest. Worship happens elsewhere.
new: My home can be a place of prayer, especially when life outside is hard.
try: Set up a small prayer corner at home today, even just a folded mat facing qiblah.

title: Wealth and splendor were used to lead people astray.
subtitle: Musa's dua when there was no good left in them
then: Ibn Kathir says Musa prayed this {idea}when he was certain there was no good in them{/idea}, angry for the sake of Allah. One reading explains their wealth as a test: {trap}those misguided would think it was given because Allah loved them.{/trap}
now: A rich, famous person lives openly against Allah, and the comments say: look how blessed they are. {trap}Wealth is not proof of Allah's pleasure.{/trap} It can be a test, for them and for the one watching.
old: If someone is rich and successful, Allah must be pleased with them.
new: Wealth can be a test, not a sign of His love.
try: When you envy someone's riches today, say: may Allah bless them, and give me what is good for me.

title: Your prayer is answered, so stay on the straight way.
subtitle: What to do after a dua is accepted
then: Ibn Kathir notes Musa prayed and {reward}Harun said amin{/reward}, so the dua is called theirs. Allah answered, then commanded: {idea}as I answered your prayer, remain steadfast on My command{/idea}, and do not follow those who do not know.
now: The job offer came. The baby was born healthy. The visa arrived. You prayed for months. {idea}Now is when steadfastness matters.{/idea} An answered dua is a call to stay on course, not to drift.
old: Once my dua is answered, I can ease off.
new: An answered prayer is a reason to stay steady, not to stop.
try: Think of one answered dua and keep one habit you started while waiting for it.

title: Drowning, Firaun finally said: I believe.
subtitle: The sea parts for some and closes on others
then: Ibn Kathir describes the Children of Israel trapped at the shore, saying {trap}we are sure to be overtaken{/trap}, and Musa answering {reward}my Lord is with me, He will guide me.{/reward} The sea split. Firaun followed in pride, and {trap}believed only when it could no longer benefit him.{/trap}
now: You are at your own shoreline: debt behind you, a wall of water ahead. {reward}Say what Musa said: my Lord is with me.{/reward} And whatever you keep postponing in faith, do not leave it for the last wave.
old: I will get serious about faith when I have to.
new: Faith counts while I still have a choice, not when the waves close in.
try: In one hard situation today, say: my Lord is with me, He will guide me.

title: Now? After a lifetime of disobedience and corruption?
subtitle: The reply to Firaun's last-second faith
then: Ibn Kathir says the reply to Firaun was: {trap}do you say that now, when you disobeyed Allah before{/trap} and were among those who spread corruption and misled the people? The Prophet ﷺ related that Jibril {trap}feared mercy would reach Firaun{/trap} at that moment.
now: "I will sort myself out when I am older. Hajj at sixty, then I will change." {idea}No one is promised the warning before the end.{/idea} The open door is today's door.
old: I can leave repentance for later in life.
new: Repentance is for now, while it can still change my story.
try: Repent today for one specific thing, and take one step away from it.

title: His body was kept as a sign for those after him.
subtitle: A tyrant's end preserved as a lesson
then: Ibn Abbas said some of the Children of Israel {trap}doubted Firaun's death{/trap}, so the sea cast up his body, whole, in his known armour, onto high ground. Ibn Kathir says it was {idea}proof that Allah is All-Powerful.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ fasted Ashura in thanks for that day.
now: You feel small next to someone who holds power over you. Remember the king who claimed to be a god, {idea}washed up on the shore for everyone to see.{/idea} Power ends. Signs remain for the attentive.
old: Those with power over me are untouchable.
new: All power ends, and the end of tyrants is a sign for those who notice.
try: Look up when the next day of Ashura falls, and plan to fast it.

title: They were given a good home, then split after knowledge came.
subtitle: Division that came despite clear knowledge
then: After Firaun's fall, Allah {reward}settled the Children of Israel in an honorable place and gave them good provision.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says {trap}there was no reason for disputes, since Allah had sent them knowledge.{/trap} He cites the hadith warning this Ummah too will split, and the saved are {idea}those upon what the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were upon.{/idea}
now: Your local community has a mosque, teachers, books, even apps. Yet the WhatsApp group is split over small things. {trap}More knowledge did not stop the division.{/trap} Look at your own part in it.
old: Divisions happen because people do not know enough.
new: Division often comes after knowledge, from the heart, not the head.
try: In one disagreement with a fellow Muslim today, choose unity over winning.

title: The truth has come from your Lord, so do not doubt.
subtitle: Earlier scripture bears witness
then: Ibn Kathir links this to the verse that the Prophet ﷺ is {idea}found written of in the Tawrah and Injil.{/idea} He says those with the earlier Books {trap}knew this as surely as they knew their own children{/trap}, yet some hid it. The address ends firm: {reward}the truth has come from your Lord.{/reward}
now: A question pops up that you cannot answer, and you feel your faith wobble. {idea}You are allowed to ask, read, and look for evidence.{/idea} The verse points you toward answers and away from staying stuck.
old: Having a question means my faith is weak.
new: When doubt comes, I look for the truth, which is already there from my Lord.
try: Write down one question about your faith and ask a knowledgeable person about it this week.

title: Do not be among those who deny Allah's signs.
subtitle: The loss that comes with denial
then: Right after the reassurance against doubt, the next warning follows: {trap}do not be among those who belie Allah's signs.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes some who had clear evidence {trap}still did not believe.{/trap} That, the verse says, is the real loss.
now: You notice a sign: a verse that answers what you were worrying about, a reminder at exactly the right moment. Then you shrug it off as coincidence. {idea}Pay attention to those moments.{/idea}
old: Losing means failing in money or career.
new: The biggest loss is turning away from Allah's signs after seeing them.
try: Today, when something reminds you of Allah, stop and say subhanallah instead of shrugging.

title: Some hearts have closed so far that they will not believe.
subtitle: When the word of Allah comes due
then: Ibn Kathir says these are people who {trap}did not believe despite clear evidence{/trap}, so the word of Allah came due on them. He compares it to Musa's dua against Firaun: {trap}they will not believe until they see the painful torment.{/trap}
now: Each time you ignore a reminder, it gets easier to ignore the next. The reverse is also true. {idea}Each time you respond, your heart softens a little more.{/idea} You are building it today.
old: My heart is how it is. I cannot change it.
new: My responses to Allah's reminders are shaping my heart every day.
try: Respond to the next reminder you get today, a verse or an adhan, straight away.

title: Even every sign would not move them until it was too late.
subtitle: When signs are not the problem
then: Ibn Kathir cites the verse: {trap}even if We sent angels, and the dead spoke to them, they would not have believed{/trap}, unless Allah willed. Their belief would only come when it {trap}could no longer benefit them{/trap}, as with Firaun.
now: You have watched a dozen reminder videos this month, nodded at each, and changed nothing. {trap}The next video will not do it either.{/trap} One small action will do more than another sign.
old: One more reminder and I will finally change.
new: It is not signs I lack. It is a willing heart and one first step.
try: Skip the next reminder video today, and act on the last one you already watched.

title: One whole town turned back in time.
subtitle: The people of Yunus and their repentance

row.title: sincere repentance
sub: Allah saw the truth in hearts

then: Most nations denied their Messengers. Ibn Kathir notes that between Musa and Yunus, no whole nation believed except the people of Yunus in Nineveh. When they saw signs of the warned punishment, {idea}they humbled themselves and cried to Allah{/idea}, Qatadah said for forty nights. {reward}Seeing their sincerity, Allah removed it from them.{/reward}
now: The test results come back worse than you expected. Suddenly you are making dua in the hospital car park, crying in a way you have not cried in years. {trap}You think it is too late to start now.{/trap} {reward}Sincere turning, even at the edge, is seen.{/reward}
old: I left it too long. Allah will not accept me now.
new: A sincere, humble return can change what seemed certain.
try: Make one dua today with your whole heart, as if your town depended on it.

title: Will you force people to believe?
subtitle: Faith cannot be pushed into a heart
then: The Prophet ﷺ longed for everyone to believe. Allah tells him that had He willed, all on earth would have believed, {idea}but He has wisdom in what He does.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites verses like {trap}you do not guide whom you love{/trap} and your duty is only to convey.
now: Your teenage son has stopped praying. You lecture him in the car, at dinner, through his bedroom door. {trap}Each time he closes off more.{/trap} {idea}You can remind, love and pray. The heart is not yours to force.{/idea}
old: If I push hard enough, they will believe.
new: I am a reminder, not a controller. Hearts belong to Allah.
try: Replace one lecture you planned today with a dua for that person, made privately.

title: Belief comes by His leave, and needs a thinking mind.
subtitle: Guidance and the use of reason
then: No soul believes except by Allah's permission. Ibn Kathir explains that He places {trap}disorder and misguidance{/trap} on those who do not reason about His proofs and evidences. {idea}He is Just in all of it{/idea}, guiding whom He wills.
now: You scroll past a clip about how the body heals a cut, or how a seed knows which way is up. {trap}You swipe without a thought.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks you to stop and reason.{/idea}
old: Faith and thinking are separate things.
new: Using my mind on Allah's signs is part of being guided.
try: Spend five minutes today really thinking about one thing in your body you never made.

title: Look up. Look around. The signs are everywhere.
subtitle: An invitation to observe creation

row.title: an open heart
sub: signs do not help the unwilling

then: Ibn Kathir lists the signs: {idea}stars, sun and moon, night and day trading length, rain bringing dead earth to life, animals, mountains, the sea carrying ships.{/idea} Yet {trap}neither signs nor warners benefit those who will not believe.{/trap}
now: Tonight the sun will set at a slightly different minute than yesterday. The rain on your window will feed a tree you will never see. {trap}You will probably be looking at a screen.{/trap} {idea}Look up once.{/idea}
old: If Allah showed me something, I would believe more.
new: He is showing me all the time. The question is whether I look.
try: Go outside at sunset today and watch it for two full minutes.

title: What exactly are you waiting for?
subtitle: Waiting like those before them

row.title: waiting to see
sub: delay until it is too late

then: Ibn Kathir explains the question: are those who reject the Prophet ﷺ {trap}waiting for days like those when earlier nations were punished?{/trap} He is told to answer calmly: {idea}then wait, I am waiting with you.{/idea}
now: You say you will get serious about faith after the wedding, after the exams, after the kids grow up. {trap}You keep waiting.{/trap} {idea}Ask yourself honestly what the waiting is for.{/idea}
old: I will change once the right moment comes.
new: Waiting is not neutral. It is a choice with an ending.
try: Pick one change you keep postponing to a someday. Start a tiny version today.

title: Saving the believers is a promise He made.
subtitle: A right Allah placed on Himself
then: After the warning comes the promise: {reward}Allah saves His Messengers and those who believe.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}this is a right Allah made binding on His Noble Self{/idea}, like His saying that He has written mercy for Himself.
now: The bills are piling up. The diagnosis is uncertain. You are trying to stay upright in faith, but some nights it feels like no one is holding you. {reward}Allah promised to save the believers. He does not break promises.{/reward}
old: Holding on to faith may not make any difference in the end.
new: Allah has bound Himself to save the believers. My faith is not wasted.
try: Write down one promise of Allah you know. Read it tonight before you sleep.
