title: If you doubt my faith, here it is plainly.
subtitle: I worship the One who takes your life
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to say to people in doubt: {trap}I do not worship what you worship besides Allah.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: I worship Allah alone, {idea}the One who causes you to die just as He gives you life{/idea}, and to Him is your return.
now: A coworker asks why you step out at lunch to pray. You mumble something vague. {trap}You are not sure how to say it.{/trap} {idea}It can be simple: I worship the One who gave me life and will take it.{/idea}
old: My faith is private. I do not need to say what I believe.
new: When asked, I can state it simply and without apology.
try: Write one clear sentence that explains your faith. Keep it ready for when someone asks.

title: Set your face straight, toward Him alone.
subtitle: Being hanif, turned away from partners
then: The command continues: direct your face toward the religion, as a hanif. Ibn Kathir explains it as {idea}making one's intention in worship solely for Allah{/idea}. A hanif is one who {trap}turns away from associating partners with Allah.{/trap}
now: You give in charity and then post about it. You pray at the front so people see. {trap}Part of your face is turned to the audience.{/trap} {idea}Straighten it. Do one deed with no audience at all.{/idea}
old: As long as I do good deeds, who sees them does not matter much.
new: Good deeds are meant to face Allah alone, not the crowd.
try: Do one good deed today that no one will ever know about.

title: Do not call on what cannot help or harm you.
subtitle: Turning to powerless things

row.title: Allah alone
sub: harm and benefit in His hand

then: The Prophet ﷺ was told not to invoke besides Allah what can neither benefit nor harm. Ibn Kathir notes the challenge: {trap}call on them to harm me, and you will see they can do nothing.{/trap} {idea}Only Allah holds harm and benefit.{/idea}
now: Before the interview you touch your lucky ring, check your horoscope app, text the friend who always says it will be fine. {trap}You call on everything but Him.{/trap} {idea}Ask Allah first.{/idea}
old: Small superstitions are harmless comfort.
new: Turning to powerless things for help pulls my heart from the One who has power.
try: Before your next stressful moment, make a short dua before anything else.

title: No one can lift what He sends, or block His good.
subtitle: Harm and favor both come from Him

key.label: Who to fear and hope in

then: Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}good, evil, benefit and harm come from Allah alone{/idea}, so only He deserves worship. The verse ends with His names: Forgiving, Merciful. {reward}He forgives whoever turns to Him in repentance, whatever the sin.{/reward}
now: You hear a rumor that a colleague is trying to block your promotion. You lie awake running scenarios. {trap}It feels like they hold your future.{/trap} {reward}If Allah wills good for you, no one can turn it away.{/reward}
old: Someone else can block what is meant for me.
new: No one can hold back the good Allah sends me, or lift a hardship but Him.
try: Name the person you fear most right now. Tell Allah about it, then let them go from your mind.

title: The truth has come. What you do with it is yours.
subtitle: Guidance is for your own soul
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to announce that the truth has come, with no doubt in it. {reward}Whoever is guided benefits himself{/reward}, and whoever strays suffers against himself. Ibn Kathir explains he said: {idea}I am not a guardian over you. I am only a warner. Guidance belongs to Allah.{/idea}
now: You think of your prayers as something you give Allah, like a bill you pay. {trap}On tired days you resent it.{/trap} {reward}Every prayer lands in your own account. He does not need it. You do.{/reward}
old: Being religious is something I do for Allah.
new: Every step of guidance is a gift to my own soul.
try: Before your next prayer, tell yourself: this is for me. Notice if it feels different.

title: Follow what was revealed. Be patient. He will judge.
subtitle: The closing instruction of the surah
then: The surah closes by telling the Prophet ﷺ to {idea}hold to what Allah revealed and be patient with the opposition he met.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: until Allah judges between you and them. {reward}He is the best of judges, in His justice and wisdom.{/reward}
now: You are doing the right thing at work and getting mocked for it. Your family does not understand your choices. {trap}You want it resolved this week.{/trap} {idea}Keep following. Keep patient. The verdict is not yours to rush.{/idea}
old: If I am right, I need to be proven right soon.
new: My part is to follow and be patient. Allah will judge, and He judges best.
try: Pick one ongoing conflict. Decide to stop arguing it today and leave the outcome to Allah.
